text:
Gustav Forsling's goal against Detroit on Wednesday, a wrist shot NHL.com called "brilliant," was a reminder of what the box score has been hiding. The two-time Cup winner, a waiver claim who became Florida's most trusted defenseman, has only three points in 20 games. Our numbers say the quiet start is mostly about who finishes the chances, not about how he is playing.

He is logging over 21 minutes a night, and the ice tilts Florida's way when he is out there: the Panthers have taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on, more than four points better than without him. That is the same profile Evolving-Hockey liked last season, when he was worth 0.9 wins while drawing the other team's best players. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he stopped 16% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%). His points pace sits below the bottom of our range for him, after 26 assists last season. The Panthers have won seven of their last ten.
headline: Gustav Forsling's quiet points hide a strong start
